hot.title: Training Reasoning Models in Simulation to Natively Use Real Robots
hot.summary: The authors train a robot-use model with reinforcement learning on simulated tasks, using task-success rewards and a shared end-effector pose interface. The model observes camera images and robot state, then proposes each move. It reaches 74.4% on LIBERO and succeeds in 18 of 30 real YAM trials, versus none for its base model; evidence is limited to tested tasks.

hot.title: Unbundling Multimodal Vision Encoding
hot.summary: The authors compare multimodal model designs by separating visual pretraining, dedicated vision capacity, and where image processing occurs, while controlling data and compute. At the longest budget for a 1.7B backbone, in-fusion reaches 49.2% Avg. VQA, versus 48.9% for a scratch encoder and 44.8% without dedicated vision processing. These dense-backbone experiments do not rule out benefits from external data.

hot.title: K2-Horizon: A Frontier Fleet of Open Source Language Models
hot.summary: K2-Horizon releases six models with checkpoints, logs, training data, and code. The authors train four dense and sparse models on a shared 22-trillion-token corpus; their normalized loss curves nearly overlap, though normalization aligns endpoints. At final mid-training, 36B-A4B scores 86.9 on 0-shot MMLU versus 88.1 for dense 32B, with about one-seventh as many active backbone parameters per token.

hot.title: Stream of Belief: Eliciting Collective Intelligence through Latent Belief Dynamics
hot.summary: Stream of Belief treats multi-agent reasoning as repeated exchange and revision of continuous internal beliefs. Agents alternate global interaction, using other agents’ beliefs, with local refinement based on their own belief and the problem; belief tokens mix embeddings from the top 50 candidate tokens. On GPQA-Diamond, SoB scores 44.9% versus LatentMAS’s 34.3%, below debate’s 53.0%.

hot.title: ScaleVLA: Scaling Vision-Language-Action Models to 552 Billion Parameters
hot.summary: ScaleVLA connects a frozen 552-billion-parameter vision-language backbone to a trainable action head, which converts image, instruction, and robot-state features into action chunks without generating text. In fixed-budget benchmarks, it reaches 87.8% LIBERO-Goal success with 10 demonstrations per task, versus 85.6% for a 2B policy with 50. Its comparisons do not isolate parameter count from model-family differences.

hot.title: Gamer: A Generalist Vision-Language-Action Foundation Model for Long-Horizon Real-Time Game Agent
hot.summary: Gamer is an agent for long quests in Honkai: Star Rail, using keyboard-and-mouse control with task instructions and memory summaries. It combines continued pre-training, supervised fine-tuning, and online reinforcement learning across finite interaction segments, using game-verified outcomes. On two held-out quests in the same game, Gamer-RL raises milestone-based accuracy over Gamer-SFT; these are not full-quest completion rates.

hot.title: Envisioning Agentic Robotics: A New Era of Robotic Systems
hot.summary: The authors present Embodied System 2, a framework in which a foundation model and embodied harness interpret intent, call robot capabilities, and verify physical outcomes. In RT-Safe, eight VLMs had 91.3% completion in paused simulation versus 94.1% in real time, but safe success fell from 19.8% to 0.7%; timing alone was not isolated.

hot.title: Weight-Space Reading
hot.summary: The authors test whether a reader can predict behavioral effects of model-weight edits without running the target, comparing access to weights and Python tools with text descriptions of the same edits. On subtle edits, the 27-billion-parameter reader scores 0.730 balanced accuracy with weights versus 0.578 with text alone. This result rests on 10 changed edits and 18 changed behavior labels.

hot.title: Weight-Space Programming Doesn’t Need Transformers
hot.summary: The paper studies WSP, where an LLM writes another model’s weights directly, without gradient training. The authors let LLMs choose model structures; three writers independently produce sparse fact tables. Claude Opus 5.5’s first-generation table reaches 50.8% ARC accuracy with 0.94 million parameters, about 1,800 times fewer than the 1.72-billion-parameter Qwen3-1.7B model written by that writer. The finding is limited to untrained models and multiple-choice recall.

hot.title: SLAM Dunk: A Recipe for Long-Horizon Egocentric SLAM in the Wild
hot.summary: SLAM Dunk improves offline visual–inertial bundle adjustment by allowing stereo-camera calibration to vary over time and fitting gyroscope scale and axis-misalignment errors. On the held-out LaMAria leaderboard, it exceeded Aria in three of five categories, including Medium (78.9 versus 78.5 CP), but its equally weighted category mean was lower (75.46 versus 75.86). This supports near-parity on the benchmark, not an overall win.

hot.title: EviBridge: Encoding Predictive Visual Evidence for Proactive Interaction
hot.summary: EviBridge gives a streaming vision-language model a second visual evidence stream that preserves when and where observations occurred, using information available at each decision time. E-RecentHist scores 0.6448 Overall on FuGIBench, versus 0.2178 for E-Native, which lacks its evidence interface and alignment stage. This supports the full system, not an isolated V-JEPA 2 effect, on staged synthetic episodes.

hot.title: The Flip Test: Video World Models Fail to Learn the World State
hot.summary: FlipTest evaluates whether video models change predictions across physical tipping points. It compares near-identical starting scenes, matched controls, and simulated sweeps to test whether predictions track the feature that changes the outcome. Across 11 tested models, Gemini Omni Flash 1.1 achieves 18.3% Level 1 pair accuracy, below the 25% binary-guessing reference; all tested video models score below 25% on simulation.

hot.title: World Intelligence Agent: Unifying World Modeling and Action Learning for Digital Agents
hot.summary: WIA presents a world model that predicts a digital agent’s next response from its interaction history and action. It uses a shared action–observation interface and evaluates predictions across seven domains, with out-of-domain tests limited to sources or benchmarks within those categories. On WIA-Bench, its 122B-A10B model scores 57.35 versus 53.19 for Kimi-K3 under the judge and a different training recipe.

hot.title: MMFlash: Faster Speculative Decoding for Vision-Language Models
hot.summary: MMFlash adapts DFlash’s parallel block-diffusion drafter for vision-language models by weighting training toward image-dependent tokens the drafter predicts poorly. It uses sparse attention to reduce the drafter’s context for long videos. On Qwen3.5-9B ChartQA, it achieves 3.58× decoding speedup versus DFlash’s 3.20×, with greedy decoding in its test setup.

hot.title: MovieRoll: A Systematic Framework for Rolling Out Long-Form Videos
hot.summary: MovieRoll generates continuous videos across prompted events by jointly denoising neighboring chunks and selectively retaining historical attention states. It trains a multi-step base with windowed training, then distills it into a five-step generator. On the 60-second, six-event HeliosBench task, MovieRoll-Distilled scores 6.492 versus 5.880 for Helios-Base; MovieRoll-Base was not evaluated at this duration, and generation remains below real-time playback.

hot.title: Latent Feedback Is a Compute and Data Amplifier: Scaling Law for Latent Feedback Transformers on Repeated Data
hot.summary: The authors test latent feedback, which passes each token’s top-layer state into the next token’s input, against a repeated-data Transformer. At matched validation loss, it uses 48% less compute (60M, 400 UTPP, two epochs) and 41% less unique data (271M, 100 UTPP, three epochs). It can lose when data is scarce; evidence covers one recipe, dataset and model ladder.

hot.title: JVT: Just Video Transformer makes pixel-space video diffusion simple
hot.summary: JVT asks whether video can be generated directly from pixels without a pretrained autoencoder. It uses a large-patch Transformer to predict clean video from noisy pixels and can jointly predict RGB and aligned disparity for camera-conditioned generation. On UCF-101, it reports FVD 136.5 versus Latte’s 477.97 at 256 × 256 on 16-frame clips. On RealEstate10K, joint RGB-disparity improves translation and AUC metrics over RGB-only, with a small increase in FVD; these camera results are specific to the reported 8-frame setup.

hot.title: Accelerate Bench: Evaluating Agents for Application-Level Program Optimization
hot.summary: Accelerate Bench evaluates whether agents can speed scientific-computing workflows while preserving outputs. Tasks specify workloads and correctness constraints but leave optimization choices to agents, who can revise code and settings. On version 1.1, Claude Sonnet 5.5 scored 67.4% in one run. A QiboTN replay found deferred loading helped only with broad dispatch in the tested program and circuits.

hot.title: Calpha: Toward Native Biomolecular Intelligence in a General-Purpose Language Model
hot.summary: Calpha connects a chat model’s residue states to a structure generator, letting it choose text or structure output. ESM2-3B features and a conditioning front-end pass Qwen’s states to a SimpleFold-3B head. On CASP16 domains, mean Cα TM-score is 0.635. On 300–600-residue chains, Calpha scores lower than a direct ESM2 baseline; differing training recipes prevent attributing the gap to Qwen alone.

hot.title: StreamEmbed: Real-Time Indexing from Pixels for Screenshot Retrieval
hot.summary: StreamEmbed indexes screenshot histories for later visual retrieval by removing redundant blocks and reusing cached computations across screenshots. On the held-out SME-H1 benchmark, its Qwen3-VL-2B index reaches 82.1 Recall@10 at 0.66 seconds per screenshot, compared with 83.4 at 2.33 seconds for the full-screenshot index. Across three histories, it is 2.8–3.7 times faster, within 1.3 points, on an M2 Pro GPU.

likes.title: An Energy-Based Perspective on Machine Learning
likes.summary: The tutorial presents energy-based models as a framework for understanding and composing machine-learning methods. Each method is described through its energy representation, inference procedure, and learning process; adding energy terms can combine requirements and reuse separately learned components. Examples in planning and toy sampling illustrate this approach, but do not establish reliable composition or generalization in arbitrary tasks.

likes.title: Interpretable Weight-Space Programming Builds Transparent Transformers and Brain Encoding Models
likes.summary: iWSP lets a coding agent write interpretable model features directly and revise them using a fixed evaluator’s score, rather than learning feature weights through backpropagation. In brain encoding, the evaluator fits ridge-regression readouts. The visual model outperforms interpretable baselines on held-out data in early and ventral cortex, but trails AlexNet in ventral cortex; story-position features also reveal scan-edge timing.

likes.title: UGG: Unified Generative Geometry Model
likes.summary: UGG unifies video generation and geometric prediction by completing aligned RGB, depth, and camera-ray representations from observed scene components. A shared multimodal model treats observed tokens as context and denoises missing ones; test-time search ranks candidate completions using image-derived evidence. On RealEstate10K with only endpoint images, search lowers translation-direction angular error from 8.260° to 3.475°, but verification is imperfect.

likes.title: A Theory of Policy Optimization in Post-Training: Coverage Collapse and Reference Resets
likes.summary: The authors introduce Approximate Policy Mirror Descent (APMD), which repeatedly resets the KL-regularization reference to the latest policy and makes strongly regularized local updates. They define response coverage as the average reciprocal probability of generating an optimal response. In a constructed bandit, REINFORCE needs exponentially many gradient steps, while stylized PPO-NoClip has a polynomial bound under softmax-linear policies and linear rewards.

likes.title: Ropedia Xperience 2: A Gold Standard for Scaling Physical AI Environments and Behaviors
likes.summary: Ropedia Xperience 2 combines real scene scans with head-mounted human task recordings, registering video and estimated motion to the scan. The captures support simulated scenes and robot policy rollouts. In one converted home simulation, a robot completed an eight-step mug-to-microwave-to-bedroom task from all 30 held-out start states. This demonstrates simulated success for one task, not real-world performance or a scaling law.

likes.title: Back to Pixels: Lifting Latent Video Diffusion into Pixel Space
likes.summary: PixVid adapts a pretrained video diffusion transformer to generate pixels one frame at a time, replacing temporally compressed VAE latents with pixel patches. It predicts clean video and aligns controls to individual frames, avoiding block waits. On text-to-video generation, it scores 84.78 VBench versus 84.05 for Wan2.1, while control latency falls from 495 ms to 34 ms at lower throughput.

likes.title: Classical Energies Learn to Reason 1,000x Faster than Looped Models
likes.summary: CRAM (Compact Reasoning Associative Memory) learns a pairwise energy over candidate puzzle boards and searches for low-energy solutions rather than repeatedly predicting digits. It guides cell-by-cell search while keeping clues fixed. It solves 99.996% of 412,786 Sudoku-Extreme test puzzles, with 282-fold fewer inference FLOPs than EBR at matched accuracy; these structured-puzzle results do not establish general reasoning ability.

likes.title: Beyond the Training Distribution: A Survey of Reasoning Generalization in Large Language Models
likes.summary: The authors survey how large language models generalize reasoning procedures across explicit distribution shifts. They organize methods by whether they act during training, inference, or architecture, and review behavioral, mechanistic, and theoretical evidence. The survey finds that methods can help in particular settings, but none consistently generalizes across shifts; differences among studies preclude controlled comparisons.

likes.title: OnlyAct: Extracting Action Representations from Foundation Models for World Models
likes.summary: OnlyAct learns action representations from unlabeled video to condition video world models and transfer demonstrated motion across scenes. It adapts a pretrained V-JEPA 2 encoder with contrastive frame-pair examples, while real-action control still needs labeled examples. On unseen RLBench video-generation transfer, it scores 0.686 in transfer direction versus 0.572 for DreamDojo; this is offline, not closed-loop control.

likes.title: Knowledge Distillation for Language Models: A Survey of Training Contexts and Supervision
likes.summary: The survey organizes language-model distillation by training-context provenance and version lag, distinguishing external, current-policy, lagged-policy, and mixed-policy supervision. It separates context origin from supervision and update choices, and uses LM-KD to compare seven scenarios. In one reported Qwen3-8B example, Lightning OPD cuts GPU-hours from 120 to 30, but this does not establish a general advantage for reused contexts.

likes.title: LoopFill: Pipelined Multi-Token Speculative Decoding for Looped Transformers
likes.summary: LoopFill accelerates looped-model decoding by combining retrieved continuations and shallow-loop predictions in one draft tree. These guesses start later token computations early, while full-depth verification selects tokens and preserves the autoregressive output distribution. Under greedy decoding, decode-latency speedup averages 5.85× across seven benchmarks for Ouro-2.6B, versus 4.19× for LoopAhead; it does not measure end-to-end throughput.

likes.title: Dataset Distillation via Drifting
likes.summary: The authors introduce dataset distillation that optimizes class distributions in frozen feature spaces rather than classifier losses. Synthetic images are pulled toward real examples and separated from one another across augmented views. With ten noise-initialized images per ImageNet-1k class, a ResNet-18 reaches 27.0 ± 0.2% top-1 accuracy, versus 11.7 ± 0.3% for the strongest noise-initialized baseline; the results do not establish lower overall compute.

likes.title: Actor, Judge, or Teacher? Understanding Decision Models in Long-Horizon Agents
likes.summary: JEV uses one fixed decision model as Actor, Judge, and Teacher: it scores rollout actions after the trajectory, and centered scores augment GRPO outcome advantages during training. For Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct, Hindsight + Progress raises ALFWorld All success from 72.8% ± 3.6 to 82.9% ± 2.9, and WebShop success from 56.8% ± 3.8 to 71.4% ± 0.7, in two text environments with episodes capped at 30 and 15 actions, respectively.

likes.title: Optimization principles, revisited
likes.summary: The authors present a quantitative framework for testing whether biological systems approach performance limits under explicit constraints. Insect lens sizes across species follow a predicted tradeoff between geometric resolution and diffraction, within a rough model. A fly-motion estimator is correlator-like for common natural inputs, not evidence of neural implementation. In a receptor-array model, random layouts lose a few percent of modeled information.

likes.title: LEASH: Stay Safe in Agentic Robotics
likes.summary: LEASH adds model-agnostic safety checks between planner and robot, reviewing goals, proposed actions, and selected operations in visual context. For GPT-6 Astra in RoboRisk-S simulation, it reduced task-averaged Harm Rate from 11.23% to 0.00% and raised Safe Success Rate from 78.99% to 80.80%. This result covers one planner in simulation; it does not establish that LEASH eliminates harm.

likes.title: Singularity-Bench: Can Agents Build Agents?
likes.summary: Singularity-Bench tests agents’ ability to build systems across six phases of AI development. Agents receive minimal code and fixed work budgets; their systems are compared with mature references on the same hardware. Among 11 agents, Opus 5.5 with Claude Code is the only one reported to match or beat references on all six tasks, with a Singularity-Index of 1.251. The benchmark is a proxy for recursive self-improvement, not a full test.
